subject: Scaling surge alignment — renewal smoothing & procurement timing

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ramos <s.ramos@helixa.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 4 Jun 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Scaling surge alignment — renewal smoothing & procurement timing

Sofia — thanks again for the time earlier. Quick summary and three options to make the upcoming growth window predictable for Helixa while keeping procurement tidy as you head into renewal:  

1) Short-term Burst Slab (one-off): add a burst capacity slab that covers x3 baseline traffic for 4 weeks, priced as a one-time add-on. No change to renewal term.
2) Smoothing Credit + Co-term: apply a smoothing credit that offsets peak consumption and align the contract to a March co-term (annualize remaining months).
3) Hybrid: small reserved top-up + burst slab with a modest blended discount for the burst portion, and a single co-term amendment.

Attached is a pricing matrix with ballpark math for each path — it shows unit economics at 2.5x and 3.0x traffic and the resulting invoice impact. If you can confirm (a) expected peak multiplier, (b) preferred co-term target, and (c) procurement owner, I can draft a scoped amendment and a SOW for legal/finance.

Attachments: [Attachment: Helixa_Pricing_Matrix_v3.xlsx], [Attachment: Redwood_Proposal_v2.pdf]

Two asks: 
- Can you confirm whether the surge window is Aug 1 — Aug 28?
- Are you looking to co-term to Mar 31, 2027 or stay on your current anniversary?

I’ll loop in Ben (discount approval) and Laura (ops/timing) once you confirm the path.

Thanks —
Markus Klein

Markus — thanks, the three-option breakdown is helpful. Quick answers: 
- Peak: we expect ~3x baseline for roughly 4 weeks, target window Aug 1 — Aug 28.
- Co-term: we'd prefer to co-term to Mar 31, 2027 if the math works (keeps our quarter-end clean).
- Procurement owner: procurement@helixa.com (they own PO/DocuSign).

Budget is tight — we need a path that caps cash outflow in Q3. A smoothing credit that reduces the Q3 hit would be ideal. Please include an option that spreads cost into Q4 if possible. Attached our internal PO template for your legal team.

Attachment: [Attachment: Helixa_PO_template.pdf]

—Sofia
VP, Platform Partnerships
Helixa
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 4 Jun 2026 12:01:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Scaling surge alignment — renewal smoothing & procurement timing

Team — forwarding Sofia's note. Helixa expects ~3x for 4 weeks (Aug 1–28) and wants to co-term to Mar 31, 2027. Budget sensitivity: they want to avoid a big Q3 cash hit; smoothing/spread into Q4 is preferred.

My suggested commercial levers (numbers in attached revised matrix):
A) Burst Slab: one-time add-on at list with a small (10%) promotional discount on slab units. Pros: no contract change; Cons: Q3 invoice spike.
B) Smoothing Credit + Co-term: shift some of the burst cost into a credit applied across remaining months after co-term (approx 30% of burst value applied as smoothing credits) plus co-term to Mar 31, 2027. Requires Amendment + Finance ok.
C) Hybrid: reserve a small top-up (25% headroom) priced at a discounted reserved rate + burst slab for overflow (burst billed at 50% of list for first x% over headroom). Net blended discount ~18–22%.

I think option B best balances Helixa's ask and Redwood revenue predictability. Need Ben/Revenue sign-off and Kimberly to confirm invoicing cadence (spread into Q4). Priyom, can you flag any provisioning constraints for a 4-week x3 surge starting Aug 1?

I’ll prepare a short amendment draft for legal once we align on discount level and smoothing mechanics.

[Attachment: Helixa_Pricing_Matrix_v3.xlsx — updated with three commercial paths]

—Markus
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 4 Jun 2026 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Scaling surge alignment — renewal smoothing & procurement timing

Markus — I support Option B (Smoothing Credit + Co-term) with a cap: up to 30% smoothing credit against the calculated burst overage, and co-term to Mar 31, 2027. We can approve a blended concession not to exceed a ~20% revenue equivalent hit vs list for the burst portion, conditional on receiving a PO by 2026-07-15.

Finance will need the amendment language that spells out (1) credit amortization schedule, (2) invoice timing and deferral mechanics, and (3) how we account for true-up if surge < 3x. Laura/Finance to finalize payment spread.

—Ben
Head of Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
